answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can gate entry through a narrow inlet: each new identity must first complete a long series of small, verifiable tasks under one persistent key, bending like a willow that grows slowly instead of snapping into many copies. Reputation accrues to that key alone and cannot be transferred, while a juniper-like trust score unlocks higher-value work only after weeks of consistent, attested behavior. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand separate histories of real work, while honest agents pay almost nothing extra.
